items.title: MakeMyTrip and Cleartrip Both Just Launched Creator Programs. The Models Are Different — For Now
items.summary: Two near-identical launches in five weeks prove that creator-led travel commerce is here. The hard part now is proving that a reel can turn into a booking, and deciding how much the companies are willing to spend before they have that proof.

items.title: Skift Data & AI Summit 2026 Roundtable: When AI Knows Travelers Better Than Brands Do, Who Owns the Relationship?
items.summary: What happens when an AI assistant knows a traveler better than the brands competing for their business? At Skift Data + AI Summit 2026, industry leaders explored how AI is redefining personalization, trust, and the path to purchase.

items.title: India’s Next Hotel Boom Is Being Built by Companies That Don’t Run Hotels
items.summary: As developers race to own hotel assets, hospitality brands with their 'asset-light' and 'asset-right' strategies seem content managing them.

items.title: Going it Alone: Why Hotel Owners Are Dropping The Big Brands
items.summary: Franchise agreements, like casinos, tend to favor the house. Now, as a generation of hotel contracts begin to expire, some owners are deciding to walk away from the table.

items.title: California Poaches NYC’s Tourism Chief Ahead of 2028 Olympics
items.summary: Julie Coker is leaving NYC Tourism after less than two years. She needs to turn around sluggish inbound tourism and needs to move fast: Los Angeles is hosting the 2028 Olympic Games.

items.title: Fewer Flights, Higher Fares, More Travelers: The July 4 Squeeze
items.summary: Going into what is expected to be a busy July 4 travel season, airlines are cutting capacity as they hope to hold onto their pricing gains.

items.title: Delta Makes Moves to Catch Up With United in the Pacific
items.summary: Delta has spent much of 2026 building up its presence in Asia partly in an attempt to gain more market share in the Pacific from its major rival in the region, United.

items.title: One of the Largest Cash Piles in OTA Travel Sits … Largely Stuck
items.summary: Trip.com’s financials are the clearest single document in travel for understanding what “China risk” actually looks like when it shows up in a balance sheet.
